newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 21.

text.p: PRAVO - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said that he does not expect any crown devaluation or revaluation.
- The Minister of Transport, Martin Riman, expects an investment of 120 billion crowns on highways by the year 2002.
- Plzenska Banka does not intend to take part in the government-approved prevention program, where the Czech National Bank is to take over bad loans to small banks.
- Up to 32 percent of the shares of Aero Vodochody will be publicly trading on the stock market within two years.

- While only 30 percent of the SPT Telecom phone network was digital by the middle of October, 80 percent should be digital by the year 2000 and the remainder will be digitalised by 2002, according to Telecom's Press spokesman, Evzen Stanek.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Nomura International intends to invest in Investicni a Postovni Banka and purchase the shares in the bank currently held by the state. Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus called this interest in the bank "incredibly positive news."
- Health insurance companies should be given enough room to begin competing again, according to the secretary of the Ministry of Health, Miroslav Macek.
- The number of deaths was higher than the number of births in all regions of the Czech Republic in the first half of 1996. The population decreased by 5,137 in this period.
- Ceska Rafinerska a.s., the monopoly fuel producer, has posted a gross profit of approximately 700 million crowns in the first nine months of this year.

- The National Property Fund is offering a significant block of Medicamenta a.s., the leading Czech distributor of medicine and health technology. Shares with a value of 37.08 percent of the basic capital will be available for block trading starting October 25.
- Strojimport a.s. should post a turnover of 1.35 billion crowns this year, with only 100 million crowns due to imports.
